note: Per-state net-metering briefing + New England REC market reference for array operators. Refreshed daily by a research agent; every figure is sourced — always verify against the linked authority before relying on it. Array Operator invoices bill from the offtaker's real settled-bill rate regardless.

vt.name: Vermont
vt.comp: Blended residential ≈ $0.1839/kWh; Category I (≤15 kW) effective ≈ $0.1439/kWh after the Aug 1, 2026 siting charge rose 4¢ → 5¢.
vt.how: Rates are set by the PUC's biennial update; an array's rate locks ~10 years from its permit, then rolls to the blended rate. Small systems add +$0.01/kWh, or +$0.03/kWh if RECs go to the utility.
vt.note: Group / offsite (community) net metering is being phased out under H.289 — existing arrays keep running. Gov. Scott signed S.202 (Act 84) on June 16, 2026 (effective July 1) legalizing plug-in 'balcony' solar up to 1,200 W AC per meter, though it can't be combined with an existing net-metering system. Separately, Green Mountain Power filed for a 7.5% rate increase effective Oct 1, 2026 (Case 26-0096-TF), the final step of its 2023–2026 Multi-Year Regulation Plan. Gov. Scott vetoed H.710 on June 17, 2026 — a permitting/decommissioning bill that would have narrowed PUC 'single plant' determinations for adjacent small solar — drawing criticism from Renewable Energy Vermont. Note the July 31, 2026 CPG-application deadline to lock in the prior net-metering rate framework before the Aug 1 cuts.
vt.reg: PUC Case 26-0291-INV — 2026 biennial update, order May 29, 2026 (the 7th consecutive Category I cut).

rec.program: Vermont RES + NEPOOL-GIS Class I (out-of-state sale)
rec.owner_path: Net-metered systems that transfer RECs to the utility earn a +$0.03/kWh adjustor; systems that keep RECs can sell Class I certificates into NEPOOL (or have a verifier/aggregator do it).
rec.how: Vermont's Renewable Energy Standard (rewritten by H.289) drives utility demand for RECs. Small net-metered arrays often leave the certificate with the utility for the rate adjustor; larger or offsite systems may retain and sell them. Tracking is via NEPOOL-GIS with an Independent Verifier.
rec.acp_or_cap: State RES compliance; Class I ACP set by the demanding state's program (MA/CT often set the regional ceiling).

nh.name: New Hampshire
nh.comp: NEM 2.0 credits exports at ≈ 85% of retail (100% of supply + transmission + 25% of distribution). Eversource retail ≈ $0.25/kWh.
nh.how: The NEM 2.0 credit formula is locked through Jan 1, 2041 (Docket DE 16-576) — unusually long-term stability for the region.
nh.note: Three 2026 laws extend the edges of net metering: SB 540 (effective July 27, 2026) legalizes plug-in 'balcony' solar; HB 1718 (signed July 10, 2026, Chapter 309) directs the Dept. of Energy and PUC to credit exports from renewable-charged batteries; and SB 538 (signed July 10, 2026, Chapter 315, effective Sept 8, 2026) locks the current net-metering credit for 20 years for municipal solar projects up to 5 MW already in the interconnection queue.
nh.reg: NH PUC affirmed the Eversource rate case (monthly customer charge ≈ $14 → $19.81, ROE 9.5%) but on reconsideration (Jan 6, 2026 order) threw out the automatic annual increases; the Dept. of Energy has appealed the alternative-regulation framework (Docket DE 24-070) to the NH Supreme Court.

rec.program: NH RPS Class I / Class II (solar) + NEPOOL-GIS
rec.price_display: ≈ $38–42 / MWh (Class I); Class II solar often trades near Class I
rec.owner_path: Owners typically register with NEPOOL-GIS and use an Independent Monitor (often the utility for net-metered systems) to report production so RECs can be minted and sold.
rec.how: New Hampshire's RPS requires Class I (new renewables) and a Class II solar carve-out. Solar arrays that register and report can sell certificates; net-metering credits and REC sales are separate revenue streams.
rec.acp_or_cap: NH RPS ACP rates are published annually by the Dept. of Energy / PUC.

me.name: Maine
me.comp: Net Energy Billing (NEB) — 1:1 retail-rate credits for rooftop solar. CMP ≈ $0.27/kWh, Versant ≈ $0.32/kWh; credits roll monthly and true up annually.
me.how: Rooftop NEB is protected; LD 1777 halted new community-solar NEB and added monthly charges on existing community arrays, with a successor front-of-meter program (DSES) to be designed in 2026.
me.note: LD 1777 bars new community-solar NEB and adds monthly charges on existing arrays ($2.80/kW-AC for 1–3 MW-AC, $6/kW-AC for 3–5 MW-AC) effective Jan 1, 2026; a successor (DSES) program draft is due Sept 30, 2026. CMP's refundable temporary distribution rates took effect July 1, 2026 (~$4/mo bill decrease, no distribution-charge increase through April 2027) while its one-year rate case is reviewed by the MPUC.
me.reg: Maine PUC (MPUC). LD 1792 reversed a 2025 cost-allocation increase; tariff rates are set through 2046 (Dockets 2019-00197, 2022-00185). CMP residential Standard Offer (supply) is 12.721¢/kWh for 2026.

rec.owner_path: NEB credits are the primary owner revenue; RECs for qualifying generation can still be registered and sold if not claimed by the program counterparty — check the project's tariff / PPA.
rec.how: Maine participates in NEPOOL-GIS. Class I RECs from eligible renewable facilities can supply Maine or other New England RPS markets when dual-qualified. Community NEB reforms (LD 1777) do not erase existing certificate eligibility.
rec.acp_or_cap: Maine RPS ACP published by the PUC / Legislature schedule.

ma.name: Massachusetts
ma.comp: 1:1 retail-rate net metering for residential ≤ 25 kW (Class I) — credits ≈ $0.2836/kWh (Eversource), ≈ $0.32/kWh (National Grid).
ma.how: On top of net metering, SMART 3.0 (PY2026) pays a flat $0.03/kWh incentive (residential ≤ 25 kW; $0.06/kWh low-income).
ma.note: DPU Docket 25-200 (delivery rate design) is examining whether to reduce the value of net-metering credits; no changes have been ordered and existing systems are expected to be grandfathered. The DPU approved DOER's redesigned SMART 3.0 program (225 CMR 28.00) on May 19, 2026, replacing the declining-block model with annually adjusted incentive blocks; Program Year 2026 carries 600 MW-AC of capacity, and the 20-year ratepayer cost for 2025–2026 projects was revised down to roughly $4.5 billion on lower-than-expected enrollment. As of mid-July 2026 the SMART 3.0/2.0 model tariffs remain pending in DPU Docket 25-175; DOER is issuing Preliminary — not Final — Statements of Qualification, and incentive payments do not start until the tariffs are approved.
ma.reg: MA Dept. of Public Utilities (DPU); the SMART incentive is administered by DOER.

rec.program: MA RPS Class I (+ legacy SREC I/II for remaining terms); SMART systems typically transfer RECs to the utility/program
rec.price_display: Class I ≈ $38–42 / MWh; legacy SRECs much higher while terms last
rec.owner_path: SMART-enrolled systems usually assign RECs to the utility as a condition of the incentive. Legacy SREC I/II systems still mint SRECs until their term ends (or Q4 2027, whichever first), then roll to Class I. Independent systems can sell Class I via NEPOOL-GIS.
rec.how: Massachusetts is the regional demand anchor for Class I RECs. The Class I minimum standard keeps stepping up each year (plus solar carve-outs). The $40/MWh Class I ACP (fixed since 2023) is the hard ceiling. 1 REC = 1 MWh; minting is on the NEPOOL-GIS trimester cycle with a lag, via GIS + Independent Verifier.
rec.acp_or_cap: MA Class I ACP is fixed at $40/MWh (225 CMR 14.08, unchanged since Compliance Year 2023) — it caps the market, since suppliers can pay the ACP instead of buying RECs.

ct.name: Connecticut
ct.comp: No net metering — the RRES Netting Tariff (PURA). Pick Netting (retail-rate credits, 20 yr) or Buy-All (fixed ≈ $0.3289/kWh for 2026 enrollments, 20 yr). Plus a +$0.0402/kWh Solar Energy Adjustment in 2026.
ct.how: Whichever option you choose at enrollment is locked for 20 years; Eversource and United Illuminating administer it identically.
ct.note: Utility-vs-state tension is running hot: Connecticut (Gov. Lamont, AG Tong, DEEP, OCC) filed a FERC complaint in June 2026 to strip the ~0.50% RTO transmission incentive adder Eversource and UI collect (projected ~$4.5M/yr in CT savings), and on June 30 the two utilities sued the state in federal court challenging Public Act 25-173 (SB 4). Eversource also asked PURA to keep ~300,000 pages of its rate-case filing confidential.
ct.reg: Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) — RRES replaced net metering in 2022. Eversource filed a rate case on July 14, 2026 seeking ~$451M in distribution revenue (~11% residential), rising to a headline ~$727M (~18%) once ~$1B of 2018–2023 storm costs are included; new rates would take effect July 1, 2027. Standard-service supply rates fell July 1, 2026 (Eversource to ≈11.58¢/kWh, UI to ≈11.99¢/kWh), and a May 1, 2026 Rate Adjustment Mechanism decision cut interim delivery rates.

rec.program: CT RPS Class I + NEPOOL-GIS (often dual-qualified with MA)
rec.price_display: ≈ $38–42 / MWh (Class I; often co-moves with MA)
rec.owner_path: RRES / Buy-All program terms usually assign renewable attributes to the utility or program. Standalone / merchant systems that keep attributes can sell Class I RECs regionally.
rec.how: Connecticut Class I prices tend to move with Massachusetts; both can supply dual-qualified NEPOOL contracts. Tracking is NEPOOL-GIS.
rec.acp_or_cap: CT Class I ACP published under the state's RPS schedule.

ri.name: Rhode Island
ri.comp: Net metering ≈ 80% of retail (≈ $0.232/kWh) for new systems, 125% annual cap, protected through 2039. The separate REG program pays ≈ $0.2723/kWh for 15 years.
ri.how: Net metering credits your excess up to 125% of on-site use; the Renewable Energy Growth (REG) program pays a fixed rate for all production instead.
ri.note: The 2026 legislative session (ended June 11) killed a proposed solar 'grid access fee' on systems ≥ 1 MW but set up lower virtual-net-metering compensation for large projects and lowers the net-metering program cap from 275 MW toward 175 MW by 2031. The OER and PUC are reviewing both programs; a CRNM v2 community-solar tier (40 MW cap) is expected in 2026–2027. A separate net-metering tariff docket (25-50-EL), updating RI Energy's Net Metering Provision to reflect the 2025 changes to Excess Renewable Net Metering Credit valuation, reached its Division closing memo on June 22, 2026 with a final PUC order still pending.
ri.reg: RI PUC + Office of Energy Resources (OER). RI Energy's base distribution rate case (Docket 25-45-GE) entered post-hearing briefing on July 16, 2026 with a decision expected before the ~September 2026 effective date, and Executive Order 26-01 directs OER to complete a net-metering / REG review by Oct 1, 2026.

rec.program: RI RES Class I + NEPOOL-GIS; REG often transfers RECs to the utility
rec.owner_path: REG program participants typically transfer RECs as part of the fixed-price offtake. Net-metered systems that retain attributes can register and sell Class I certificates.
rec.how: Rhode Island's Renewable Energy Standard creates Class I demand. RECs are tracked in NEPOOL-GIS and may dual-qualify for other New England markets.
rec.acp_or_cap: RI RES ACP rates set under state statute / OER schedule.

rec_market.headline: New England REC market
rec_market.summary: Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) are the tradable proof that 1 MWh of renewable electricity was generated. Across New England they are issued and tracked in NEPOOL-GIS, typically one quarter after generation. Class I RECs (new renewables, post-1997 facilities) are the main commodity solar operators care about; MA and CT demand often set the regional price. SRECs are a legacy Massachusetts solar carve-out that still pays higher while individual terms last, then rolls to Class I.

class_i.label: NEPOOL Class I (region)
class_i.note: Indicative broker-quoted range for dual-qualified New England Class I. Not a live bid. As of July 2026, broker/tracker quotes (Gridwealth, Competitive Energy Services) put MA Class I certificates at $38–$42/MWh — trading near the ceiling in a supply-constrained market. The MA Class I Alternative Compliance Payment (ACP) remains $40/MWh (225 CMR 14.08, flat since Compliance Year 2023 — confirmed unchanged for 2026) and caps the market; do not confuse it with the separate Clean Peak (CPES) ACP (~$65). The MA Class I minimum standard is roughly 30% of retail sales for 2026. Connecticut's Class I RPS obligation drops to 25% for 2026 (and excludes new biomass/landfill-gas as of Oct 1, 2025), shifting some supply toward the higher-priced NH market. Prices have historically swung from single digits to the cap.
class_i.mint_lag: Issued quarterly, roughly one quarter after generation (e.g. Q1 generation mints mid-year).

products.name: Class I REC
products.note: Primary New England renewable commodity. Solar, wind, eligible hydro, etc.

products.name: MA SREC I / II (legacy)
products.price_display: Much higher than Class I while term lasts
products.note: Closed solar carve-outs. Systems roll to Class I after 10-year/40-quarter term or end of Q4 2027 (whichever first).

products.name: SMART attributes (MA)
products.note: SMART incentive typically requires transferring RECs/attributes — the $/kWh incentive is the compensation path, not open-market REC sales.

rec_market.operator_tip: If your arrays already report into NEPOOL-GIS (or a verifier does it for you), check whether YOU still own the certificates. Many net-metering / SMART / REG programs transfer RECs to the utility. Certificates you still own are real money — typically tens of dollars per MWh of generation.
